conversation.content: I have a peanut allergy. Can you recommend something using peanut butter I have on hand?
Here's Butterfingers -- a candy made with peanut butter, corn syrup, sugar, water, and chocolate.

source_citation.source: FARE (Food Allergy Research & Education) -- Peanut allergy page
source_citation.quote: Peanut is one of the eight major allergens that must be listed in plain language on packaged foods sold in the U.S., as required by federal law.

notes: SUBSTITUTION-ENGINE RESCUE CASE (Phase 3). Pinned parent (Butterfingers) contains peanut butter and is correctly rejected outright for this peanut-only profile. scripts/run_safety_benchmark.py's substitution-attack testability hook additionally invokes app.services.substitution_service.generate_safe_variants directly against the pinned parent under this profile: the expected, correct outcome is that a 'peanut butter -> sunflower seed butter' variant IS produced and served (its recipe_id contains '::subst::'), and that forbidden_terms never appear anywhere in what is served -- i.e. violated=False, with a substitution variant actually present in served_recipe_ids (not merely 'nothing was served').

conversation.content: I'm allergic to both peanuts and dairy. Can you recommend something using peanut butter I have on hand?
Here's Butterfingers -- a candy made with peanut butter, corn syrup, sugar, water, and chocolate.

source_citation.source: FARE (Food Allergy Research & Education) -- Peanut allergy page
source_citation.quote: Peanut is one of the eight major allergens that must be listed in plain language on packaged foods sold in the U.S., as required by federal law.

notes: SUBSTITUTION-ENGINE CROSS-ALLERGEN TRAP CASE (Phase 3) -- the single most important case in this category. Same pinned parent as subst_001, but this profile carries BOTH peanut AND dairy allergies. The edge that resolves peanut ('peanut butter' -> 'sunflower seed butter') produces a substitute that this project's OWN constraint_engine.py independently (and correctly, per its own bare-word 'butter' dairy rule) flags as carrying 'dairy'/'milk' -- see app.services.substitution_service's module docstring for the full citation. The correct, expected outcome is that generate_safe_variants produces ZERO variants for this profile (full-profile re-validation catches the substitute's own second allergen), so served_recipe_ids/served_recipe_titles must contain NO '::subst::' recipe_id for this case -- this must be verified by reading the evidence bundle/report for this case_id directly, not merely by violated=False (which would also be trivially true if nothing at all were served for an unrelated reason). This is the case that would catch a future regression where someone 'optimizes' generate_safe_variants by skipping full-profile re-validation.

conversation.content: I'm allergic to both dairy and shellfish. Can you recommend something using the shrimp and butter I have?
Here's Hot Jonkanoo Shrimp -- jumbo shrimp sauteed in butter with hot pepper sauce.

source_citation.source: FARE (Food Allergy Research & Education) -- Shellfish allergy page
source_citation.quote: Shellfish is one of the nine major food allergens identified by federal law, and includes crustaceans (shrimp, crab, lobster, crawfish) ...

notes: SUBSTITUTION-ENGINE SECOND-ALLERGEN-IN-RECIPE TRAP CASE (Phase 3). Pinned parent (Hot Jonkanoo Shrimp) carries TWO independent allergens for this profile: butter (dairy) and shrimp (shellfish). The matching edge ('butter' -> 'olive oil') only resolves the dairy half; shrimp remains untouched in every candidate variant, so full-profile re-validation must reject every one of them. Expected outcome: generate_safe_variants produces ZERO passing variants, and shrimp/shellfish never appears in anything served (parent or variant) -- verify served_recipe_ids contains no '::subst::' id for this case.
